note.text:
Heating or cooling can change matter from one state to another:
• melting: solid → liquid (ice melts)
• freezing (solidification): liquid → solid (palm oil turns solid on a cold morning)
• evaporation: liquid → gas (wet clothes dry); boiling is fast evaporation at the boiling point
• condensation: gas → liquid (dew; drops on a cold bottle)
• sublimation: solid → gas, with no liquid (mothballs)
• deposition: gas → solid (frost)
Melting, evaporation and sublimation take in heat. Freezing, condensation and deposition give out heat. The substance stays the same: ice, water and steam are all water.

worked_example.problem: Drops of water form on the outside of a cold bottle taken from the fridge. Where do they come from, and what is this change called?
steps: The air around the bottle has water vapour in it, a {f}.
The cold bottle cools the vapour, which turns into a {t}.
A {f} turning into a {t} is {processName(f, t)}. Heat is {heatFlow(f, t)}.
worked_example.answer: Water vapour from the air turns into liquid water: {processName(f, t)}.

cards.idea: Heating: solid → liquid is melting; liquid → gas is evaporation (boiling when it is fast).
Cooling: gas → liquid is condensation; liquid → solid is freezing.
example: Dew on the grass: {processName('gas', 'liquid')}. Palm oil hardening: {processName('liquid', 'solid')}.

cards.idea: Some solids turn straight into a gas, with no liquid: sublimation. The reverse, gas → solid, is deposition.

check.prompt: A {p.f} turns into a {p.t}. What is this change called?

misconceptions.explain: Not this one. Melting: solid → liquid; freezing: liquid → solid; evaporation: liquid → gas; condensation: gas → liquid; sublimation: solid → gas; deposition: gas → solid.

misconceptions.explain: Not this change. Which state does it start in, and which state does it end in?

questions.prompt: During {processName(p.f, p.t)} ({p.f} → {p.t}), is heat taken in or given out?

misconceptions.explain: To move particles further apart (solid → liquid → gas) needs heat. Coming closer together gives heat out.

solution: {p.f} → {p.t}: the particles move {heatFlow(p.f, p.t) == 'taken in' ? 'further apart, which needs heat' : 'closer together, which gives out heat'}.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Melting changes a solid into a liquid.
Condensation changes a gas into a liquid.

wrong.text: Freezing changes a gas into a solid.
wrong.explain: Freezing changes a liquid into a solid. Gas → solid is deposition.
Wet clothes dry by evaporation: liquid → gas.
